clue.text: Lie related by stupid on purpose

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled and senseless, so these three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells a foolish fib on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' is the anagram signal: the twelve letters of LIE RELATED BY rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on purpose means doing it intentionally, with forethought: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Attractive daughter on a diet

parts.note: a table can mean the food provided at meals, as in 'keeps a good table', so it stands for diet

explanation.surface: A good-looking girl is slimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces; TABLE as diet is the older sense of the food one regularly eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone datable is appealing enough to go out with, so the word serves as a casual synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Fast time over, then slow

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
O is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A musical direction: speed up, then the tempo drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a tempo marking opposite to the definition, but it means going without food; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian musical direction telling players to perform at a slow pace.

clue.text: Money namely consumes Queen supporter

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: to consume something is to take it inside, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: IE (id est) is the abbreviation meaning namely
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Cash, as it happens, ends up spent on a royal patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' makes IERE; 'supporter' looks like a royal backer but is a humorous name for underwear, and ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, an undergarment whose job is to support the bust, hence a humorous supporter.

clue.text: Initially rush around in dawn attack

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A military assault at daybreak, troops charging about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of rush, around, in and dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden surprise attack, the kind classically launched at dawn: a synonym.

clue.text: Abstinent support nearly everybody downing dram

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece downing another sits below it, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: a tee is the small peg that supports a golf ball
a tot is a small measure of spirits, like a dram

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's nightmare: almost everyone knocking back whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downing' looks like drinking but places AL (ALL with 'nearly' dropping a letter) below TOT; TEE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person never drinks alcohol, so they are abstinent: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sign of artist supporting party member

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece holds the other up from beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of that political party
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter's symbol backing a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac: an example.

clue.text: Terrible time to swallow popular banter

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the combined word encloses the other piece

parts.note: bad means terrible
an age is a long period of time
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A dreadful stretch of having to accept what is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' applies to the two adjacent words together, not to 'time' alone, giving BADINAGE once the popular word sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful exchange of teasing remarks, the same thing as banter.

clue.text: Person that is offensive

definitions.note: here a noun, a military offensive, matching the noun answer

parts.note: a sort is a person, as in 'a good sort'
IE (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Someone who is rude or objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as an adjective but is the noun for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sally by troops from a defended position, a form of military attack.

clue.text: Tease, at least in pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, signalling these words are made into a mess

explanation.surface: Mild flirtation, at the very least while wearing underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is the anagram signal for AT LEAST IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something held just out of reach, which is a form of teasing.

clue.text: Live ace? Not really for party

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
A is the card abbreviation for ace
a reply of 'not really' amounts to no

explanation.surface: Is it a genuine star performer? Not exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a lively celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Top of black bug

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
a louse is a small parasitic insect, a bug

explanation.surface: The tip of a dark insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like part of the insect but is a garment; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse is a woman's shirt-like garment worn on the upper body, a top.

clue.text: Mass said first for Puritan

parts.note: M is the physics abbreviation for mass
oral means spoken, said
1st written with I for 1 gives IST

explanation.surface: A religious service spoken before anything else, for a strict Protestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service but is the physics symbol; 1st is read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist preaches strict ethics, like a puritan in the lower-case sense of a stern prude.

clue.text: English jobs losing right for responses

indicators.note: losing something means dropping it, so a letter goes from the word

parts.note: chores are jobs about the house

explanation.surface: British employment falls without the right reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are reflected sounds coming back, and figuratively replies, so they are responses.

clue.text: Hear a gun shot broadside

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of these words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Listen to the cannon fire a broadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but signals the anagram of HEAR A GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal attack, as is a harangue: a long ranting tirade.

clue.text: Male digger's first tool for plant

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a rake is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A gardener's main implement for growing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a Mediterranean plant with a forked root, the subject of folklore.

clue.text: Insecure party, American, accepting outrage

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: a do is a party
anger is outrage

explanation.surface: An unstable political group from the US taking in public fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous is unsafe and full of risk, which insecure can also mean.

clue.text: Autocratic of French position in charge

parts.note: de is French for of
a spot is a position

explanation.surface: A dictatorial French official with his rank and command.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler wields absolute power, as an autocrat does: a synonym.

clue.text: Butcher regarding famous horse being rejected

indicators.note: rejected is read as sent back, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: re means regarding, about
Red Rum was a racehorse that won the Grand National three times

explanation.surface: A meat seller dismisses a story about a celebrated racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: REREDRUM read backwards gives the answer; the horse's name famously reverses to MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to slaughter brutally, so a butcher in that sense is a murderer.

clue.text: Parrots make half cut bird sounds

indicators.note: with half cut away, only the first two of the four letters remain

parts.note: caws are the harsh cries of crows

explanation.surface: Parrots imitate, chopping bird calls in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' could be a verb (copies) but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large, brightly coloured tropical American parrots: an example.

clue.text: Queen formerly admitting former attachment

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Anne was a British queen of the early 18th century
ex means former

explanation.surface: A past monarch confesses to an old flame.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an attachment or extension.

clue.text: Bend or seizure grips back

indicators.note: the phrase grips the answer, holding it inside its letters across the words

explanation.surface: A bent spine or a fit seizes the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' seems part of the medical picture but is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or approve, which is what backing someone means.

clue.text: Some edifice, not a pharaoh's tomb

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monument that is not an Egyptian king's burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial in the form of an empty tomb, honouring those buried elsewhere.

clue.text: Stray got in making cat cross?

indicators.note: stray means wandering off course, so these letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A stray wandered in, making the cat angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' links; 'cross' looks like angry but means a hybrid, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a cross between big cats.

clue.text: Sold stolen goods getting confined

definitions.meaning: to fence is to deal in stolen property

explanation.surface: A receiver of stolen goods ends up locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a criminal dealer in loot, and a fenced area is enclosed by barriers.

clue.text: Search round old valley

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Hunting about an ancient dale.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, a word found in southern England.

clue.text: Mature split with sweetheart

parts.note: a rip is a split or tear
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A grown-up breaks up with a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but is the centre letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe fruit is fully developed, ready to eat, which is what mature describes.

clue.text: Extorted perhaps, seeing wife called

parts.note: rung is the past participle of ring, to call by phone

explanation.surface: Blackmail, maybe, once a spouse phoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example; 'seeing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Money wrung from someone is squeezed out by force, so extorted is one sense.

clue.text: Standard used by many European states

definitions.text: Standard used by many European states

parts.words: Standard used by many European states
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and several European nations such as France, Italy and Ireland fly three-colour ones

explanation.surface: A norm adopted across much of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a common rule but means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A national flag of three bands, like those of France or Italy, carries this name.

clue.text: Remote cabin with less ice around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A distant hut with less frost about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal and covers all three words; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote place is far away and hard to reach, which is what inaccessible means.
